note: The raw PoC bytes are passed to the HTTP/1 fuzz harness as the client request stream.
The harness forwards the same byte buffer and size to the writer thread feeder.

code: char *p = (char *)memmem(buf + pos, len - pos, MARKER, sizeof(MARKER) - 1);
note: The PoC contains the harness marker, so only the request prefix is written before the client-side loop waits.
The written prefix is an HTTP/1.0 request for the registered reverse proxy path /reproxy-test.
The reverse-proxy upstream responds with HTTP/1.0 200 OK and closes.
When the upstream closes, the buffered final response body state is detached for the proxy generator.
For an empty final buffer, the proxy final send uses a zero send-vector count.
The zero vector count is propagated to the generic response send path as a final send.
The generic send wrapper forwards the same zero bufcnt to the output stream chain.
On a later body-state call after headers have already been emitted, the HTTP/1 final stream can retain bufcnt as zero.

code: h2o_socket_sendvec(conn->sock, bufs, bufcnt, h2o_send_state_is_in_progress(send_state) ? on_send_next : on_send_complete);
note: The unchecked zero bufcnt is passed into the socket send-vector routine.
UBSAN reports a non-positive VLA bound when cnt is zero.
